Rashi on Berakhot 50a:12:1.hebrew: ואידך - עוברים ממקור נפקא, ואנן ממקהלות דרשינן:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:12:1.english: And the other [Sage] - [The matter of] fetuses is derived from "from the source," and we expound from "in assemblies."

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:13:1.hebrew: הלכה כר"ע - בבהמ"ז, דאחד עשרה ואחד עשרה רבוא:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:13:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva - In Grace after Meals, that [the formula is the same for] both ten and ten myriads [one hundred thousand].

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:14:1.hebrew: מברכינן תלתא תלתא - ריש גלותא מאריך בסעודתו, ואנן, כל ג' וג' שגמרו סעודתן מזמנין בקול נמוך, ויושבין אחר הברכה עד שגמר ריש גלותא ויזמנו הוא והיושבין אצלו בקול רם. ולקמן פריך: וניפקו בברכה דריש גלותא:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:14:1.english: We recite the blessing in groups of three - The Exilarch would prolong his meal, and as for us, each group of three that finished their meal would recite the zimmun in a low voice, and remain seated after the blessing until the Exilarch finished and he and those sitting beside him recited the zimmun in a loud voice. And later on, [the Gemara] asks: And let them fulfill [their obligation] through the blessing of the Exilarch?

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:14:2.hebrew: שמע ריש גלותא - אם היו מזמנין י' י', היה צריך המברך להגביה קולו, וישמע ריש גלותא ויחרה לו שאנו עושין חבורה לעצמנו בפרהסיא. אע"ג דמפקי נפשייהו מידי זמון של הזכרת השם, וכי הדר מזמן ריש גלותא בהזכרת השם לאו אינהו נפקי ביה, כדאמר רבה תוספאה דאין זמון למפרע — אפ"ה ניחא להו בהכי, משום דאוושי כולי עלמא, שהיו שם מסובין רבים ואין קול המברך נשמע:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:14:2.english: The Exilarch would hear - If they were to recite the zimmun in [groups of] ten, the one reciting the blessing would have to raise his voice, and the Exilarch would hear and become angry that we are forming a [separate] group for ourselves in public. Even though they exclude themselves from the zimmun with the mention of the [Divine] Name, and when the Exilarch subsequently recites the zimmun with the mention of the [Divine] Name they do not fulfill [their obligation] through him — as Rabba Tosefa'a says that there is no retroactive zimmun — even so, this was preferable to them, because everyone was making noise, as there were many diners there and the voice of the one reciting the blessing could not be heard.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:15:1.english: And recited the blessing on his own - For himself, without a zimmun.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:15:2.hebrew: למפרע - משבירך, וידי זמון לא יצא:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:15:2.english: Retroactively - Once he has blessed, and he did not fulfill [the obligation of] zimmun.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:16:1.hebrew: פתיא - כלי חרס, כדאמר (ע"ז ד' לג:) הני פתיותא דבי מכסי:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:16:1.english: Pot - An earthenware vessel, as [the Gemara] says (Avodah Zarah 33b): "These pots of Bei Mikhsei."

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:16:2.hebrew: בהדי פלוגתא למה לך - טוב לך לאחוז דברי רבי ישמעאל, שאף ר"ע מודה דכי אמר המבורך טפי עדיף, אלא שאין צריך:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:16:2.english: Why do you [involve yourself] in a dispute - It is better for you to follow the words of Rabbi Yishmael, for even Rabbi Akiva concedes that when one says "the blessed One" it is all the more preferable, only that it is not necessary.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:17:1.hebrew: אינן רשאין ליחלק - דאיתחייבו להו בזמון:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:17:1.english: They are not permitted to divide - For they have become obligated in zimmun.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:17:2.hebrew: וכן ד' - אין הג' מזמנין והיחיד יחלק מהם, דאיהו נמי איקבע בחובת זמון:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:17:2.english: And so [too] four - The three may not recite the zimmun while the individual separates from them, for he too was established in the obligation of zimmun.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:17:3.hebrew: ששה נחלקים - כדי זמון לכאן, וכדי זמון לכאן:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:17:3.english: Six may divide - [Because there is] enough for a zimmun for this [group] and enough for a zimmun for that [group].

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:17:4.hebrew: עד עשרה - אבל עשרה אין נחלקים, דאיתחייבו להו בזמון הזכרת השם, עד שיהא עשרים, ואז יחלקו, אם ירצו, לשתי חבורות:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:17:4.english: Up to ten - But ten may not divide, as they have become obligated in the zimmun of mentioning the Divine Name, until there are twenty, and then they may divide, if they wish, into two groups.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:1:1.hebrew: אף ברכו - שפיר דמי, ומיהו טוב לו להיות בכלל המברכים:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:1:1.english: Even "Bless" - It is fine, but nevertheless it is better for him to be included among those who bless.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:1:2.english: We learned - [This is] support for Shmuel.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:1:3.hebrew: ששה נחלקין - אם רצו ליחלק לשתי חבורות ולזמן אלו לעצמן ואלו לעצמן, רשאין הן, שהרי יש זימון כאן וכאן:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:1:3.english: Six may divide - If they wish to divide into two groups and recite the zimmun, these by themselves and those by themselves, they are permitted [to do so], for there is a zimmun both here and there.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:1:4.hebrew: עד עשרה - כלומר, וכן ז' וכן ח' לשתי חבורות, וכן ט' לשתי חבורות או לשלשה — עד עשרה. אבל אם היו עשרה, חלה עליהן הזכרת השם, ואם יחלקו לא יהיה שם הזכרה — אין נחלקין עד שיהיו שם עשרים:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:1:4.english: Up to ten - That is to say, and likewise seven and likewise eight [may divide] into two groups, and likewise nine into two groups or into three [groups] — up to ten. But if there were ten, the invocation of the [Divine] Name took effect upon them, and if they divide there will be no invocation of the Name there — they may not divide until there are twenty there.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:22:1.hebrew: ג' שבאו משלש חבורות - וכדמסיים רב חסדא, שבאו מג' חבורות של ג' בני אדם בכל חבורה, ונתחייבו אלו בזמון, ועמד אחד מכל חבורה ונצטרפו שלשה לחבורה אחת — חייבין לזמן ואינן רשאין ליחלק, שכבר הוקבעו. ואפילו לא אכלו אלו השלשה משנצטרפו יחד, שכבר גמרו סעודתן עם הראשונים:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:22:1.english: Three who came from three groups - And as Rav Ḥisda concludes [below], that they came from three groups of three people in each group, and these [individuals] had become obligated in *zimmun*, and one [person] stood up from each group, and the three joined into one group — they are obligated to recite the *zimmun* and are not permitted to divide, since they have already been established [in their obligation]. And [this applies] even if these three did not eat [anything] once they joined together, since they already finished their meal with the first [groups].

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:2:1.hebrew: ה"ג ואי אמרת ברכו עדיף אמאי ששה נחלקין - אם ירצו — הא מעיקרא יכולין לומר ברכו, והשתא תו לא אמרי:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:2:1.english: This is the reading: And if you say [that saying] "Bless" is preferable, why do six divide - If they wish [to divide] — behold, initially they were able to say "Bless", but now they can no longer say [it].

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:2:2.hebrew: אלא לאו ש"מ - אף ברכו קאמר מתני'. וכיון דמתני' אף ברכו קאמר, מסתברא היא שטוב לו לאדם להיות מן המברכים, וסייעתא דשמואל. וגירסא הכי איתא: ששה עד עשרה, ואי אמרת ברכו דוקא, אמאי ששה נחלקין? אלא לאו ש"מ אף ברכו — ש"מ:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:2:2.english: Rather, mustn't one conclude from this - The Mishnah is saying "even: Bless." And since the Mishnah is saying "even: Bless," it stands to reason that it is good for a person to be among those who bless, and [this is] a support for Shmuel. And the textual reading is as follows: "Six [may divide] up to ten. And if you say [that the Mishnah means] specifically 'Bless,' why may six divide? Rather, mustn't one conclude from this [that it means] 'even: Bless'? Conclude from this."

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:3:1.english: It was also taught so - That the Mishnah is saying "even: Bless."

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:3:2.hebrew: והנקדנין - דווקנין תופסין אותו על שהוציא עצמו מן הכלל:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:3:2.english: And the punctilious - Exacting [people] take him to task for having excluded himself from the collective.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:3:3.hebrew: ומטובו הרי זה בור - שממעט בתגמוליו של מקום, דמשמע דבר מועט, כדי חיים:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:3:3.english: "And from His goodness," he is an ignoramus - For he diminishes the bounties of the Omnipresent, as it implies a small amount, [just] enough to sustain life.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:4:1.hebrew: בשאלה שאני - שהשואל שואל כעני על פתח, שאינו מרים ראש לשאול שאלה גדולה:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:4:1.english: In [the case of] a request, it is different - For one who asks does so like a poor person at the door, who does not lift his head to make a large request.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:4:2.english: Open your mouth wide - To ask for all your desires.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:5:1.hebrew: חיים ה"ז בור - דהוציא עצמו מן הכלל:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:5:1.english: "Life," he is an ignoramus - For he excluded himself from the collective.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:5:2.hebrew: מתני איפכא - חיים עדיף, שכולל את כל באי עולם:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:5:2.english: Taught the opposite - [The wording] 'they live' is preferable, for it includes all inhabitants of the world.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:6:1.hebrew: נברך שאכלנו משלו - משמע שהוא יחידי, שהכל אוכלים משלו:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:6:1.english: Let us bless [the One] of Whose [food] we have eaten - It implies that He is unique, in that everyone eats from His [bounty].

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:6:2.hebrew: למי שאכלנו משלו - משמע מרובים הן — זה זן את זה וזה זן את זה — ולפי דבריו מברך את בעל הבית:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:6:2.english: To the one from whose [food] we have eaten - [This] implies that they are multiple — this one feeds that one, and that one feeds this one — and according to his words, he is blessing the host.

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:7:1.hebrew: התם מוכחא מילתא - דבמעשה נסים ליכא למימר מרובין:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:7:1.english: There the matter is evident - For regarding the performance of miracles, it cannot be said [that there are] multiple [performers].

Rashi on Berakhot 50a:9:1.hebrew: כדתנן על המזון שאכלנו - ולא קתני משלו:
Rashi on Berakhot 50a:9:1.english: As we learned [in the mishna]: "For the food that we have eaten" - And it does not teach: "Of His [food]."

Tosafot on Berakhot 50a:13:1.hebrew: אמר רבא הלכה כר"ע - פירש ר"ח דהכי קיי"ל, והלכך בין בעשרה, בין במאה, בין ברבוא — אומר: "נברך אלהינו על המזון שאכלנו". אבל בג' לא יזכיר "על המזון", כדאמר לעיל. וגם בעשרה, אם אינו רוצה להזכיר "על המזון" — הרשות בידו, ואומר: "ובטובו חיינו":
Tosafot on Berakhot 50a:13:1.english: "Rava said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva" - Rabbeinu Chananel explained that this is how the halakha is established; and therefore, whether with ten, with one hundred, or with ten thousand, he says: "Let us bless our God for the food that we have eaten." However, with three, he should not mention "for the food," as [the Gemara] said above. And even with ten, if he does not wish to mention "for the food," he has permission [to omit it], and says: "and by His goodness we live."

Tosafot on Berakhot 50a:22:1.hebrew: שלשה שישבו לאכול כאחד - אף על פי שהיו חלוקין בככר, שכל אחד ואחד אוכל מככרו — אינן רשאין ליחלק. כלומר: אף על פי שהן חלוקין בככרות, וס"ד אין זה צרוף ולא חל עליהם חובת זימון — אפ"ה אינן רשאין ליחלק:
Tosafot on Berakhot 50a:22:1.english: "Three who sat to eat as one" - Even though they were divided with respect to the loaf, in that each and every one eats from his [own] loaf, they are not permitted to divide. That is to say: even though they are divided with respect to [their] loaves, and it would enter your mind [that] this is not [considered] a joining together and the obligation of zimmun does not take effect upon them — even so, they are not permitted to divide.

Tosafot on Berakhot 50a:2:1.hebrew: אלא ש"מ נברך עדיף - לאו דוקא עדיף, אלא כי הדדי נינהו. ועדיף היינו חשוב, כמו הקישא עדיף וג"ש עדיף פ' איזהו מקומן (זבחים ד' מח.) — ר"ל דההיקש חשוב, ואין לבטלו מפני הג"ש. וה"נ קאמר: נברך חשוב כמו ברכו, ולפיכך לא יוציא עצמו מן הכלל. והקונטרס מוחק עדיף; ומיהו אתי שפיר עדיף כדפי':
Tosafot on Berakhot 50a:2:1.english: "Rather, conclude from this: 'Let us bless' is preferable" - [This does] not strictly mean "preferable"; rather, they are equal [to each other]. And "preferable" means "significant," like [the expressions] "the juxtaposition is preferable" and "the verbal analogy is preferable" in the chapter [entitled] Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 48a) — meaning that the juxtaposition is significant and is not to be set aside because of the verbal analogy. And so too here, [the Gemara] means: "Let us bless" is as significant as "Bless," and therefore one should not exclude himself from the collective. And Rashi [ha-Kuntres] deletes "preferable"; but nevertheless, [the reading] "preferable" works out well as we explained.

Tosafot on Berakhot 50a:3:1.hebrew: שמש מצרפן לזמון - וה"ה בשני בתים, ובני אדם עומדים ומשמשין מזו לזו — מצטרפין. וכן איתא בירושלמי, ובלבד שישמעו ברכת המזון מפי המברך. והא דנקט במתני' "בית [אחד]" — משום חדוש דסיפא, דאפילו בבית אחד, אם לאו — אין מזמנין. וכן בבית חתנים: כשאוכלים בחופה בב' בתים, ובני אדם משמשין מזו לזו — מצטרפין, ובלבד שישמעו ברכת המזון מפי המברך:
Tosafot on Berakhot 50a:3:1.english: "A waiter combines them for zimmun" - And the same applies to two houses: where people are standing and serving from one to the other, they combine [for a zimmun]. And so it is stated in the Yerushalmi, provided that they hear the Grace after Meals from the mouth of the one reciting the blessing. And that which [the Mishnah] stated, "[in] one house" — [this is] because of the novelty of the latter clause: that even in one house, if not [i.e., if they cannot see each other], they do not form a [single] zimmun. And so too in a wedding house: when they eat for the wedding [feast] in two houses, and people are serving from one to the other, they combine, provided that they hear the Grace after Meals from the mouth of the one reciting the blessing.

Tosafot on Berakhot 50a:8:1.hebrew: על המזון הרי זה בור - דמשמע דמברך לבעל הבית המאכילו; דאי לרחמנא — למה הוא מזכיר מזון? בלא מזון יש הרבה לברכו:
Tosafot on Berakhot 50a:8:1.english: "For the food, he is an ignoramus" - For it implies that he is blessing the host who feeds him; for if [he were blessing] the Merciful One, why does he mention food? [Even] without food, there is much to bless Him for.
